findings.issue: Governance workflow references nonexistent script — always fails at runtime
findings.impact: The sole governance CI workflow runs `pwsh ./scripts/automation/run_full.ps1` which does not exist. Any governance enforcement is effectively disabled.
findings.fix: Either create scripts/automation/run_full.ps1 with intended governance checks, or rewire governance.yml to use existing scripts: evaluate_gate.py, sync_baseline.py, and hardening pipeline runner.

findings.issue: governance.json is a 6-line stub with no tier definitions, inheritance, or environment mapping
findings.impact: No tier definitions for dev vs staging vs production, no P0/P1/P2 threshold differences, no policy versioning, no inheritance model.
findings.fix: Restructure governance.json as multi-tier policy document with tiers object containing development/staging/production keys, each with block_on thresholds, required_checks, approval_gates.

findings.issue: No hotfix bypass procedure or compensating controls documented for emergency deployments
findings.impact: During critical security incidents, engineers either delay the fix (extending outage) or bypass controls unsafely without defined compensating controls.
findings.fix: Document hotfix procedure: criteria (P0 outage, active exploit), approval flow (two-person review + on-call lead sign-off), compensating controls (post-deploy monitoring, 24h reversion plan, retrospective).

findings.issue: Policy changes are not reviewable or auditable — no policy-as-code review process
findings.impact: Changes to governance.json, core.rules.json can be made without oversight. A developer could silently weaken security thresholds.
findings.fix: Add CODEOWNERS entry requiring review for hardening/policies/. Add PR template checkbox for policy changes. Add CI validation of policy file structure against JSON schema.
